syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Understanding Society India and Beyond PART-I
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: What Social Science Is and Its Place in Everyday Life
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Social Science in Everyday Life

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Social Science as the systematic study of human society and how it differs from the natural sciences.
Explain how ordinary daily activities depend on wider systems of governance, economy, society and environment.

topics.title: Understanding Society through Time and Traditions
topics.ncert_sections: Understanding Society through Time and Traditions

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how human societies changed from early communities to villages, towns and cities.
Explain how ideas such as the Panchamahabhutas, vasudhaiva kutumbakam and the Arthashastra reflect early inquiry into society.
Identify the methods social scientists use to gather evidence and build explanations.

topics.title: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines
topics.ncert_sections: Social Science as a Study of Disciplines

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a complex society must be studied from the perspectives of several related disciplines.
Identify the four core disciplines of Grades 9-10 Social Science and the wider Social Science family.

topics.title: Geography
topics.ncert_sections: Geography

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what Geography studies, including location, distribution and human-environment relationships.
Explain how Geography combines spatial and temporal perspectives in a holistic approach.
Identify the tools Geography uses, such as maps, globes, atlases and GIS.

topics.title: History
topics.ncert_sections: History

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of the itihasa-purana tradition in preserving cultural memory in Bharat.
Describe how modern historiography uses empirical evidence and scientific tools.
Classify sources of history as literary, archaeological, epigraphic or numismatic.

topics.title: Political Science
topics.ncert_sections: Political Science

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Political Science as the study of governance, power, constitutions and institutions.
Explain how early Indian political thought linked politics with dharma, artha and rajadharma.
Explain how the Panchayati Raj system shows grassroots democracy and local participation.

topics.title: Economics
topics.ncert_sections: Economics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Economics studies the use of limited resources and decisions by consumers, producers and governments.
Describe India's economic journey from a leading economy through colonial disruption to rebuilding after independence.
Explain sustainable growth as meeting present needs without harming future generations.

topics.title: Why Study Social Science and Its Future
topics.ncert_sections: Why Should We Study Social Science?; The Future of Social Science; Secondary-Stage Social Science

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how understanding government and shared challenges prepares students for responsible civic life.
Explain how Social Science accounts for diversity and the underlying unity of Indian society.
Describe the growing role of Social Science in addressing future challenges and linking past, present and future.

topics.title: Plate tectonics and the Earth's interior
topics.ncert_sections: Plate Tectonics

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the crust, mantle, core, lithosphere and asthenosphere and their key features.
Identify the types of tectonic plates and the major plates of the world.
Explain how convection currents in the mantle drive plate movement.

topics.title: Plate boundaries and their effects
topics.ncert_sections: Plate Tectonics (plate boundaries)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish convergent, divergent and transform boundaries and the features each produces.
Relate the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes, including the Ring of Fire, to plate boundaries.

topics.title: Weathering and erosion
topics.ncert_sections: Process of Weathering and Erosion

concepts.learning_objective: Differentiate physical, chemical and biological weathering.
Explain how erosion differs from weathering and how it affects human livelihoods.
Describe soil conservation practices such as contouring, bunding, terracing and the Zabo system.

topics.title: Running water and its landforms
topics.ncert_sections: Agents of Gradation; Running Water

concepts.learning_objective: Name the agents of gradation and state how they level the Earth's surface.
Explain the formation and human uses of waterfalls, meanders, oxbow lakes and deltas.

topics.title: Landforms of waves, glaciers, wind and underground water
topics.ncert_sections: Waves and Currents; Glaciers; Wind; Underground Water

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how waves form beaches, cliffs, caves, arches and stacks.
Identify glacial landforms such as U-shaped valleys, cirques, aretes, fjords and moraines.
Identify landforms made by wind and by underground water in limestone areas.

topics.title: Landforms and disasters
topics.ncert_sections: Landforms and Disasters

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the natural and human causes of landslides and avalanches.
Explain the causes of glacial lake outburst floods and dust storms.

topics.title: Composition of the Atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Composition of the Atmosphere

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main gases of the atmosphere and their approximate shares.
Explain the varying share of water vapour and its role in clouds and precipitation.

topics.title: Structure of the Atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Structure of the Atmosphere

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the layers of the atmosphere are defined and how temperature changes through them.
Distinguish the troposphere from the stratosphere by their features and uses.
Describe the mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere and the phenomena linked to them.

topics.title: Weather, Climate and Their Elements
topics.ncert_sections: Weather and Climate; Elements of Weather and Climate (temperature, humidity, precipitation)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish weather from climate.
Explain why temperature decreases from the equator towards the poles.
Explain humidity and the forms and causes of precipitation.

topics.title: Air Pressure, Wind and Local Winds
topics.ncert_sections: Atmospheric pressure; Wind; Land breeze and sea breeze

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how air pressure varies with altitude and temperature.
Define wind and name winds by the direction they blow from.
Explain the formation of land and sea breezes.

topics.title: Seasons in India
topics.ncert_sections: Seasons in India; traditional Indian seasons (Table 3.2)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the four seasons recognised by the IMD and their months.
Relate the six traditional Indian seasons to the Gregorian months.

topics.title: Monsoon
topics.ncert_sections: Monsoon

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the origin of the word monsoon and the mechanism of the south-west monsoon.
Explain the north-east monsoon and its rainfall on the south-eastern coast.
Assess the role of the monsoon in the economy and life of India.

topics.title: Climate Change and Carbon Footprint
topics.ncert_sections: Climate Change; Let's Explore: My Carbon Footprint

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the human causes and effects of climate change.
Define carbon footprint and suggest ways to reduce it.

topics.title: Punjab Floods 2025: A Case Study
topics.ncert_sections: Punjab Floods 2025: A Case Study

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the natural and human-made causes of the 2025 Punjab floods.
Analyse the effects of floods and measures to reduce flood damage.

chapters.title: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation

topics.title: The Invention of Writing: Before and After
topics.ncert_sections: The Invention of Writing: Before and After

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the earliest writing systems, including the undeciphered Harappan script, cuneiform, hieroglyphs and Brahmi.
Distinguish the periods before and after writing by their sources, share of human history and accuracy of dating.

topics.title: Early Human Evolution and Migration
topics.ncert_sections: Why Should We Study Early Human History?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain biological and cultural evolution and how surplus production laid the basis of civilisation.
Describe the dispersal of Homo erectus and Homo sapiens out of Africa.

topics.title: Our Human Ancestors and the Evidence
topics.ncert_sections: Who Were Our Human Ancestors?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why tool making marks human behaviour and identify the major human ancestors and their tools.
Explain how fossils, tools and experiments help archaeologists reconstruct the human past.

topics.title: Periods of Early History and Palaeolithic Hunter-Gatherers
topics.ncert_sections: Periods in Early Human History; Palaeolithic Hunter-Gatherers

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange the periods of early human history and identify the technology that defines each.
Describe Palaeolithic sites in India and the progression of tools from handaxes to blades and microblades.

topics.title: Mesolithic Hunter-Gatherers and the Neolithic Revolution
topics.ncert_sections: Mesolithic Hunter-Gatherers; The Neolithic Revolution; Neolithic Period in Indian Subcontinent

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a warmer climate shaped Mesolithic life, microlithic tools and art such as at Bhimbetka.
Explain the Neolithic revolution as a shift to food production through domestication.
Describe Mehrgarh and the spread of Neolithic communities in the Indian subcontinent.

topics.title: Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation: The Early Harappan Stage
topics.ncert_sections: Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the continuity of crafts and practices from the Early Harappan to the Mature Harappan stage.
Describe Harappan agricultural practices, water management and standard weights.

topics.title: Bronze Age Civilisations Outside India: Mesopotamia
topics.ncert_sections: Bronze Age Civilisations Outside India; Mesopotamian Civilisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four river-valley civilisations and explain the contacts between Mesopotamia and the Harappans.
Describe the Sumerian ziggurat, cuneiform writing and other inventions.
Trace the sequence of Akkadian, Assyrian and Babylonian power and the Code of Hammurabi.

topics.title: Egyptian and Chinese Civilisations
topics.ncert_sections: Egyptian Civilisation; The Chinese Civilisation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of the Nile, pyramids, papyrus and the Rosetta Stone in Egyptian civilisation.
Describe Chinese dynasties, oracle bones, crafts, the Great Wall and the Silk Route.

chapters.title: State and Society up to 1000 CE

topics.title: The Vedic period: sources and political institutions
topics.ncert_sections: The Beginnings; State and Administration: The Vedic Period; Political Institutions in the Vedic Period

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the four Vedas and the parts of Vedic texts and explain why historians use them as sources.
Describe the role of the raja, the janas and the assemblies sabha, samiti and vidhata in early Vedic polity.

topics.title: Janapadas, mahajanapadas and early kingdoms
topics.ncert_sections: Let's Analyse; Early Kingdoms and Republics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the shift from kin-based janas to territorial janapadas and mahajanapadas, and the forms of polity that followed.
Relate iron tools, wider crop variety and NBPW pottery to the growth of the Ganga plains.
Identify the early kingdoms of Tamilakam and their emblems.

topics.title: Duties and ideals of the king and the council of ministers
topics.ncert_sections: Duties and Ideals of the King; Council of Ministers

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the limits on royal authority and the ideal of authority over the whole subcontinent (chakravarti kshetra).
Describe Kautilya's seven constituents of the state and why they must work together.
Evaluate how inscriptions such as the Junagadh rock record help historians study administration.

topics.title: How were empires administered?
topics.ncert_sections: How Were Empires Administered?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the provincial, district and village units used in northern and southern kingdoms.
Describe the composition of the Gupta district office.
Explain how village assemblies, variyams and the Kudavolai system made villages self-reliant.

topics.title: Ethics: the foundation of law and life
topics.ncert_sections: Ethics: The Foundation of Law and Life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the principles of samatva and rita as described in early Indian texts.
Explain the meaning of dharma and how ethics guided governance from the Mauryas to the Cholas.

topics.title: Varna, jati and social mobility
topics.ncert_sections: Social Structures and Everyday Life: Varna and Jati; Social Mobility

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the origin of the varna idea and why early occupations are described as flexible.
Distinguish jati from varna and identify the factors that led to the growth of jatis.
Use inscriptions as evidence of social and occupational mobility.

topics.title: Family, women, religious life and education
topics.ncert_sections: Family and Society; Role of Women; Religious Life and the Emergence of Bhakti; The Quest for Knowledge

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the four ashramas and the four purusharthas.
Describe the roles of women in Vedic, Gupta-Vakataka, Sangam and Chola times.
Explain the rise of Bhakti in the Tamil region and its open, ritual-free path.

topics.title: Economy: agriculture, irrigation, trade and guilds
topics.ncert_sections: Economy: Agriculture and Land Revenue; Irrigation; Trade: Trade Routes and Ports; Guilds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain land revenue and the state's role in building irrigation works.
Identify the major land routes and ports that linked early Indian trade.
Analyse the economic and banking role of guilds using inscriptional evidence.

topics.title: Tracing Democratic Traditions from Early Times
topics.ncert_sections: Tracing Democratic Traditions from Early Times

concepts.learning_objective: Identify early Indian institutions such as the Sabha, Samiti, ganas and Bauddha Samghas that reflected collective decision-making.
Explain how the Constituent Assembly framed a flexible Constitution that can be amended under Article 368.

topics.title: Principles of Democracy: Popular Sovereignty, Rule of Law and Fundamental Rights
topics.ncert_sections: Principles of Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain popular sovereignty and the Universal Adult Franchise as the basis of a government's authority.
Describe equality before law, equal protection of law and procedure established by law.
Identify the six Fundamental Rights, their Articles and the remedies under Articles 32 and 226.

topics.title: Separation of Powers, Accountability, Parties and Democratic Institutions
topics.ncert_sections: Principles of Democracy; Role of Media in Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the separation of powers among the three organs creates checks and balances.
Describe how accountability mechanisms and a multi-party system make government answerable to people.
Match democratic processes with the institutions that support them, including the media as the fourth pillar.

topics.title: Types of Democracy around the World
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish direct democracy from representative democracy with examples.
Compare parliamentary and presidential systems using India, Canada, the UK, Switzerland and the USA.

topics.title: Democracy in Practice: India's Living Democracy
topics.ncert_sections: Democracy in Practice: India's Living Democracy

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret facts that show the scale and inclusiveness of Indian elections.
Explain how Panchayats, ADCs and the PESA Act enable participation at the grassroots.
Describe women's voting rights and reservation for women in local bodies.

topics.title: Challenges to Democratic Practices and Democracy and You
topics.ncert_sections: Challenges to Democratic Practices in India; Democracy and You

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse challenges such as misinformation, inequality and the Emergency of 1975-77.
Explain how informed and responsible citizens strengthen democracy.

topics.title: Why do elections matter?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between direct and indirect elections and identify offices filled by each in India.
Explain how regular, periodic and competitive elections keep representatives accountable to the people.
State the meaning and origin of the term psephology.

topics.title: The electoral system

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the First-Past-The-Post system decides the winner in a constituency.
Compare the majority (two-round) system and proportional representation with FPTP.
Apply the quota rule of the single transferable vote used for the Rajya Sabha, Vidhan Parishad, President and Vice President.

topics.title: The laws and the Delimitation Commission

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the subjects covered by the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.
Identify electoral offences and corrupt practices listed in the RPA, 1951.
Explain the purpose of delimitation in ensuring equal representation.

topics.title: Election Commission of India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the ECI as an autonomous, permanent constitutional body and the elections it conducts.
Explain how the ECI prepares electoral rolls and why it conducts the Special Intensive Revision.
Describe the ECI's functions of scheduling elections, registering parties and allotting symbols.

topics.title: Free, fair and inclusive elections: no voter to be left behind

concepts.learning_objective: Identify ECI measures that help senior citizens, PwDs and service voters cast their votes.
Match ECI digital applications such as cVIGIL, Suvidha and Saksham to their uses.
Evaluate why fairness, inclusion and trust are needed for elections to have democratic value.

topics.title: Political parties

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the roles political parties play in a multi-party democracy.
Explain defection and the provisions of the Anti-Defection Law of 1985.
Apply the ECI criteria for recognising national and state parties.

topics.title: Challenges to free and fair elections

concepts.learning_objective: Identify challenges such as misinformation, fake news and intimidation and analyse their effect on democracy.
Explain safeguards such as the Model Code of Conduct, EVMs and VVPAT.

chapters.title: Building Blocks in Economics: The Problem of Choice

topics.title: Needs, wants and economic choices
topics.ncert_sections: The Big Questions

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish needs (essentials) from wants (non-essential desires) and classify everyday purchases.
Explain that human wants are unlimited and keep changing, which makes choice necessary.

topics.title: Limited resources, opportunity cost and the PPC
topics.ncert_sections: Choices and Limited Resources

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that resources are limited and have alternative uses, so choosing one use means giving up another.
Define opportunity cost as the value of the next alternative given up.
Interpret a production possibility schedule and curve to find trade-offs and judge efficient output.

topics.title: What economics deals with
topics.ncert_sections: What does Economics Deal with?; Economic Survey

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin and meaning of the word economics and what the discipline studies.
Identify economic entities such as consumers, producers, governments and financial institutions.
Describe how economists use data, surveys and analysis of alternatives to guide decisions.

topics.title: Key questions: what to produce and for whom
topics.ncert_sections: Key Questions in Economics; What to Produce and for Whom?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how scarcity gives rise to the three key questions of economics.
Analyse trade-offs in deciding which goods to produce, such as water-intensive versus drought-resistant crops.
Explain how producers choose which group of consumers to serve based on needs and purchasing power.

topics.title: How to produce
topics.ncert_sections: How to Produce?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish labour-intensive and capital-intensive techniques of production.
Analyse the factors that decide the choice of production technique.

topics.title: Economic systems
topics.ncert_sections: Economic Systems and How Choices are Made; Planned, Market and Mixed Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how a planned economy answers the key questions through a central authority.
Describe how a market economy relies on demand and supply with limited government role.
Explain the features of a mixed economy and India's shift after 1991.

chapters.title: The Price Puzzle: What Drives the Market

topics.title: Demand and the Law of Demand

concepts.learning_objective: Define demand as willingness backed by ability to pay and state the inverse price-quantity relationship.
Derive market demand by adding individual demand schedules and interpret the demand curve.

topics.title: Other Determinants of Demand

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how price changes of substitutes and complements affect the demand for a good.
Explain how income, tastes, population, seasonality and diminishing marginal utility shape demand.
Explain how expected future prices change present demand.

topics.title: Supply and the Law of Supply

concepts.learning_objective: State the direct relationship between price and quantity supplied and the reason behind it.
Derive market supply by adding individual supplies and read the upward-sloping supply curve.

topics.title: Other Determinants of Supply

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how prices of alternative products and the number of sellers affect supply.
Explain how technology and producers' future expectations change supply.

topics.title: Market Equilibrium and Dynamic Markets

concepts.learning_objective: Identify equilibrium price and quantity and distinguish excess demand from excess supply.
Explain why real-world equilibrium keeps shifting, using examples like masks and hotel tariffs.

topics.title: Role of Government in the Economy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain price ceilings, price floors, monopoly regulation and the role of regulators.
Explain why public goods are provided by the government rather than private firms.

topics.title: Limitations of Government Intervention

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate how price distortions, compliance burdens and heavy regulation can harm markets.
